podcast.body: This is the only original song in Nirvana's discography not written or sung by Kurt Cobain; it was written and sung by Dave Grohl. Grohl wrote and recorded the song in 1990, releasing it on an indie cassette under the name Late! An alternative version was later recorded for the *In Utero* album and was included as a bonus track on the "Heart-Shaped Box" CD single. "Dave Groll's loan contribution to the Nirvana songwriting catalog Merrigold a bonus track from the heart shaped box CD single."

podcast.body: "Merrigold" is the only song by Dave Grohl to be included in the official Nirvana canon, appearing on the "Heart Shaped Box" CD single and the "With The Lights Out" box set. Originally titled "Color Pictures of a Merrigold" from Grohl's pre-Nirvana project Late, it was recorded just before Christmas 1990, with Grohl singing and playing most of the instruments, and Kurt Cobain not present on the track. "That is the only Dave girl song to ever make the Nirvana canon. He sings and he plays most of the instruments. Kurt is not even on the track."

podcast.body: Dave Grohl originally wrote and recorded this song solo in 1990, a year before joining the band. At Pachyderm Studios in 1993, he appears to have recorded it essentially alone after the others left, playing drums, singing, and likely guitar. It exists only on the CD single for "Heart-Shaped Box." "The only Nirvana song written and sung by Dave Grohl, that's our seventh weird recording."

podcast.body: Nirvana released exactly one track written and sung by drummer Dave Grohl: "Marigold," which appeared as a B-side on the CD single for "Heart-Shaped Box" (from the In Utero album, 1993). Grohl had developed considerable skills as a singer and guitarist before joining Nirvana, including time with the Washington DC band Scream. Within Nirvana, Dave essentially did what he was told. "Marigold" remains the only place to hear Grohl with Nirvana in a leading role, predating the Foo Fighters. "Long before there was such a thing as a Foo Fighter, here's Dave Grohl singing an original song with Nirvana."

podcast.body: This song, written and sung by Dave Grohl, originated as "Color Pictures of a Mera Gold" on his solo album *Pocketwatch*. A new version was recorded by Dave during the *In Utero* sessions in February 1992, with Chris Novoselic adding the bass line. Although Kurt Cobain would not allow it on *In Utero*, it was released as the last track on the "Heart-Shaped Box" CD single and later included in the *With the Lights Out* box set. The Foo Fighters have also performed it live, as documented on their *Skin and Bones* album. "It's the only Dave Roll song that ever made it with Nirvana."

podcast.body: This track, released as the second bonus track on the CD single version of "Heart-Shaped Box" in 1993, is notable as the only Nirvana song not featuring Kurt Cobain on lead vocals, and in fact, he does not play on the track at all. Written and sung by drummer Dave Grohl, he also played drums and guitars on it, with Krist Novoselic on bass. The song was re-recorded during the *In Utero* album sessions (Feb 25 or 26, 1993) but originated from Grohl's earlier solo project *Pocket Watch* as "Color Pictures of a Marigold." It holds the unique distinction of being the only track ever released by both Nirvana and the Foo Fighters (on *Skin and Bones* in 2006). "The track is called Merrigold and it was written in song by the drummer Dave Grohl"
